Subject: Sync: Retrieval design & reranker decision — next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so Polaris can start the evaluation run on your side. I kept things intentionally practical to avoid any back-and-forth.

Summary from our call:
- Primary goal: reduce hallucination in clinical note summarization while keeping 95th-pct token latency under 350ms for single-chat flows.
- Data: internal docs + 18k anonymized patient Q&A pairs (you said S3 path will be shared).
- Constraints: strict PII handling, max model footprint for dedicated instances, and a hard latency SLA for interactive UX.

Recommended evaluation plan (short):
1) Models to baseline (we'll provide prompt-suite and eval harness):
   - dense baseline: DPR dense retrieval + small cross-encoder reranker + Open-quantized 13B decode model (quantized q4) for generation
   - hybrid baseline: BM25 + dense re-rank prefilter + lightweight pointwise reranker for latency-sensitive flows
   - conservative low-cost option: quantized 7B instruct model + heavier reranker to trade accuracy for throughput
2) Retrieval configs to run in parallel:
   - sparse only (BM25 tuned on clinical stopwords)
   - dense only (precomputed vectors via your embeddings / Redwood embeddings)
   - hybrid (BM25 top-100 + dense re-rank top-100)
3) Reranker matrix to test:
   - small cross-encoder fine-tuned on your 3k annotated pairs (best accuracy, higher latency)
   - pointwise pairwise lightweight reranker (distilled) for throughput
   - neural+rules hybrid: token overlap / citation heuristics + neural score to reduce hallucination score
4) Metrics we care about (please include these in the benchmark output):
   - grounding precision (percent of answers with at least one cited doc paragraph)
   - hallucination rate (human-labeled on 500-sample probe set)
   - end-to-end latency P50/P95 under your network conditions
   - cost estimate per 1k requests under each config (tokens + retrieval ops)

Attachments: prompt-suite-v1.json (prompts we used on call), polaris_eval-benchmarks.csv (template for results), proposed-mrp-ops-plan.pdf (ops checklist for run).

Next steps we propose (dates are flexible):
- Today: Polaris shares S3 path + sample 500 records and credentials for test bucket.
- By Tue 10/19: Polaris runs three retrieval configs against the 500-sample probe and uploads polaris_eval-benchmarks.csv with raw outputs + timings.
- Wed 10/20: 30-minute readout with Polaris eval team + our engineering to pick final reranker candidate and finalize model variant.

Ben + Laura: can you confirm the exact model variant names and the minimal infra footprint (GPU memory) for the quantized 13B and 7B options? Vivek: any concerns on SLA/fallback policies we should call out to Polaris now?

Sofia — if that plan looks good, reply with the S3 path and a point person. If you prefer, we can run the initial probe here in our staging if you want to avoid sharing credentials.

Thanks,
Avery

1) Reranker latency target: for clinician-facing flows we need < 120ms additional latency budget for reranking (P95). Will the cross-encoder option exceed that?
2) For dense embeddings, we currently use a 1536-dim vector store (internal) generated from our annotation pipeline. Are Redwood embeddings compatible or should we reindex with your embeddings for parity?
3) S3: I'll share a pre-signed path to a 500-sample subset by EOD. Point person is me.

If cross-encoder is too slow for P95 we can accept slightly lower grounding precision in exchange for the distilled pointwise reranker on clinician flows; but for audit/regulatory flows (release notes, regulatory Q&As) we want the highest accuracy.

Sofia — short answers to your clarifications and concrete asks to make the probe smooth.

Reranker latency: the full cross-encoder (bi-enc + cross-attn) will typically add 200–300ms on CPU; on a small GPU-backed reranker it can meet ~100–150ms P95 depending on batch size. For your 120ms P95 target we recommend:
- Clinician UI: distilled pointwise reranker (single-forward pass) + early-exit heuristics (latency ~50–90ms P95)
- Audit/regulatory flows: cross-encoder on a small dedicated GPU (latency ~110–150ms P95) with async path and explicit QA fallback

Embeddings compatibility: you can run the probe two ways — index with your current embeddings and we run retrieval on Redwood side, or reindex with Redwood embeddings. For a controlled apples-to-apples comparison we recommend reindexing the 500-sample probe with Redwood embeddings (we provide a small script). If reindexing is hard, we will evaluate using your vectors but results may favor your dense config and make cross-config comparison noisy.

Model variants & footprints (minimal):
- Quantized 13B (q4/NH): ~18GB GPU memory on our optimized runtime; recommended for highest-quality decode with mid throughput.
- Quantized 7B (q4): ~9GB GPU memory; good throughput and lower cost.
- Distilled 3B (fast option): ~4GB; use for high concurrency but expect lower factuality at edge cases.

We will upload a short script to the Drive link that runs the three retrieval configs and writes timings into polaris_eval-benchmarks.csv. Proposed readout time Wed 10/20 10:00am PT — does that work for the Polaris team?

—Ben
